persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
at work, can't do this now.
No problem, Sam. I can either ask 2-3 quick questions by text now, or have a loan officer call you at a time that works better. Which do you prefer, and if a call, what time?
can someone call me tomorrow after 5pm?
I've booked your call, Sam. A licensed Harborline loan officer will phone you tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm.

events.name: schedule_callback

input.notes: Borrower at work, couldn't text. No qualification details collected yet; web form indicates refinance only. Confirm goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, timeline.

events.result: Callback booked. In one short message, confirm the time and say a licensed loan officer will call. Then close.

callback.notes: Borrower at work, couldn't text. No qualification details collected yet; web form indicates refinance only. Confirm goal, home value, balance, rate, credit range, occupancy, timeline.

objections.rationale: Follows the playbook. The agent acknowledged it ("No problem, Sam"), offered both options ("ask 2-3 quick questions by text now, or have a loan officer call you"), asked for a time, then booked and confirmed "tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm" without pushing.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm and use the borrower's name. Turn 4 smartly adds "(Thursday)" to remove any ambiguity. The final message ends abruptly, with no thanks or sign-off, which reads slightly transactional.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower's busy signal was respected immediately at turn 2 and the callback was booked in one exchange. Turn 4 states exactly who will call ("A licensed Harborline loan officer") and when ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm").

annotations.note: Discloses AI identity ("an automated assistant"), cites the inquiry source, and offers STOP up front.
Offers exactly the two playbook options and asks for a preferred time in one concise message.
Clarifies "tomorrow (Thursday)" and specifies a licensed loan officer will phone, so expectations are set precisely.
Closes without a courtesy such as "Thanks, Sam, talk tomorrow," so the ending feels slightly abrupt.

judge.overall_notes: Clean, compliant handling of a busy borrower that follows the playbook, with a specific, confirmed callback. The only nitpick is the lack of a polite sign-off in the closing message.
